title: Senior Commercialization Specialist, US Market - Renewable Energy
description:
**About Enfinity Global**

Enfinity Global is a purpose-driven company focused on making a positive impact on the planet by helping companies, governments, and individuals transition to a carbon-free and sustainable economy. Our role as a leading IPP is to develop, finance, build, operate, and own decarbonization assets in the long term in Europe, Asia, and the Americas through our offices in the USA, Spain, Italy, UK, Netherlands, India, and Japan.

 Our team of over 400+ Enfiniters comprises seasoned finance professionals, as well as experienced project developers and operators with extensive industry experience across all stages of the project life cycle. We pride ourselves on being creative and innovative solution providers to our customers and partners.

**Job Summary:**

Enfinity Global is looking for a Senior Specialist- Commercialization to join our Commercial Operations team and drive the commercialization of utility-scale solar PV and battery energy storage (BESS) projects across our US platform. The role owns the end-to-end preparation, coordination and submission of RFP and bid packages, supports PPA and offtake structuring, manages counterparty interactions, and tracks developments across US power markets. Based in our Hyderabad office and working as an integral part of the Enfinity Americas team, this role sits at the intersection of origination, commercial strategy, and project execution, and is suited for someone seeking direct ownership of live deals and growth at the leading edge of the energy transition. We expect this candidate to actively leverage AI and automation to improve the accuracy and efficiency of our commercial processes.

The role works closely with US-based stakeholders and counterparties, and requires a working schedule that is well aligned with US business hours.

**Key responsibilities:**

**Bid and RFP Management**

o   Lead the preparation of complete RFP, RFI and bid packages for utilities, C&I and corporate offtakers, from bid/no-bid assessment through final submission.

o   Conduct detailed reviews of solicitation documents to identify:

§  Scope, eligibility and qualification criteria

§  Submission requirements and deadlines

§  Evaluation methodology and scoring

§  Key commercial, technical and contractual nuances

o   Own the bid calendar and tracker across multiple concurrent solicitations, maintaining clear visibility on status, deadlines and open items.

o   Ensure every submission is compliant, accurate, internally approved and submitted on time.

o   Manage post-submission activity, including clarifications, shortlisting, best-and-final offers and handover to the negotiation team.

**Counterparty Management**

o   Act as the primary point of contact with utilities, offtakers, RFP administrators and independent evaluators throughout the bid process.

o   Manage bidder registrations, Q&A and clarification requests, and portal submissions.

o   Build and maintain professional relationships with counterparties and keep a clear record of all correspondence.

**Cross-functional Coordination**

o   Coordinate inputs from internal teams and stakeholders, including:

§  Finance and Capital Formation (pricing, financial models, credit support)

§  Legal (contract mark-ups, PPA terms, corporate documentation)

§  Engineering (technical design, energy yield and storage performance)

§  Development and Permitting (site control, interconnection and permitting status)

§  Construction and Procurement (EPC and equipment assumptions, schedules and costs)

o   Run bid kick-offs, working sessions and approval meetings; track follow-ups and close loops.

o   Prepare clear, defensible bid summaries for internal approval, covering key terms, pricing, risks, mitigants and decision points.

**PPA Structures and Commercial Support**

o   Apply a working understanding of offtake structures, including physical and virtual PPAs, tolling agreements, resource adequacy / capacity contracts and energy storage agreements.

o   Support Finance and Capital Formation in shaping pricing, contract term and risk-allocation positions in bid responses.

o   Review counterparty term sheets and PPA forms to flag key commercial and risk issues.

**Market Intelligence**

o   Monitor RFP and procurement activity across US power markets, including:

§  Regulated markets (vertically integrated utilities, IRP-driven procurements)

§  Deregulated / ISO-RTO markets (e.g. ERCOT, PJM, CAISO, MISO, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE)

o   Track policy, regulatory and pricing trends relevant to solar and BESS bids, including state procurement programs.

o   Maintain a pipeline of upcoming solicitations and assess their fit with the company's portfolio.

**Process & Discipline**

o   Standardize, automate and maintain bid templates, content libraries and standard documentation.

o   Leverage AI tools and automation to improve the accuracy, consistency and speed of RFP review, proposal drafting, compliance checks and bid tracking.

o   Keep CRM and bid tracking tools accurate and up to date.

o   Capture lessons learned and win/loss feedback, and proactively propose improvements to the bid process.

**Requirements**

**Experience:**

* 3-5 years of experience in commercial roles in the renewable energy sector, such as bids, tenders, RFP management, offtake or business development, with solar PV and/or BESS preferred
* Hands-on experience preparing and submitting RFPs/bids for solar PV and/or BESS projects. Experience in the US market is ideal; experience with competitive tenders in the Indian market (e.g. SECI, NTPC, state utilities, C&I) is the next best fit
* Experience with solar PV and/or BESS technology, with a good understanding of how these projects work technically and commercially, including project economics and key commercial drivers
* Knowledge of US power markets (regulated and deregulated) is a strong plus; otherwise, a clear willingness and ability to learn quickly
* Understanding of PPA and offtake structures; deeper experience in PPA structuring or negotiation will be highly valued
* Comfortable working closely with US-based teams and counterparties, on a schedule aligned with US business hours
* Advanced user of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint); working knowledge of PVsyst, CRM tools or Power BI is a plus

**Other competencies valued:**

* Clear and concise communicator, written and verbal, with the ability to draft professional proposals and correspondence
* Honesty and integrity in all interactions, both internally and with counterparties
* Proactive attitude: anticipates issues and acts before being asked
* Curious and comfortable using AI tools to work smarter, and keen to find new ways of doing things
* High accountability mindset: takes ownership, follows through and closes loops
* Highly organized and detail-oriented, able to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines
* Capacity to engage effectively with senior stakeholders and external partners

In Enfinity Global you will find a very dynamic and multinational environment in one of the most exciting and impactful industries. You will work alongside a highly experienced and collaborative team, with a clear path for growth as our US platform expands. Here we will foster your professional and personal growth, and you will have the opportunity to actively contribute and make a real impact on climate change.

title: Regulatory, Compliance & Controls Testing & Validation - Consultant
description:
**Summary**
**Position Summary**
**Regulatory, Risk & Forensic | Testing & Validation Utility**
Our Regulatory, Risk & Forensic team supports client leaders to translate multifaceted risk and an evolving regulatory environment into defensible actions that help strengthen, protect, and transform organizations. Join our team and use advanced data, AI and emerging technologies with industry insights to help client service teams bring clarity from complexity and accelerate their path to value creation.
  
  
The Testing & Validation Utility delivers integrated regulatory, compliance, and controls testing and validation services, along with regulatory reporting, across Controls Testing, Conformance Testing, Compliance Testing, Regulatory Reporting QA & Testing, Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) and Post-Effectiveness Testing, Issue Management & Remediation Validation, and Regulatory Reporting for global clients across industries, with a particular focus on Banking, Capital Markets, Investment Management, and Insurance. We expect our professionals to bring exposure across the end-to-end risk management lifecycle — Transactions, Conformance, Controls, Compliance, RCSA, and Issue Management — and to apply that breadth across the components they support.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
**Regulatory, Compliance & Controls Testing & Validation | Consultant**
**Level:**
Consultant or equivalent (4-7 years of relevant experience)
  
  
As an experienced Consultant within the Testing & Validation Utility at Deloitte Consulting Services, you will be responsible for individually delivering high quality work products within due timelines across regulatory, compliance, and controls testing and validation activities, along with regulatory reporting, spanning the Regulatory, Risk & Forensic portfolio. As needed, you will mentor and/or direct junior team members and liaise with onsite/offshore teams to understand the functional requirements.
  
  
**About**
At Deloitte, we do not offer you just a job, but a career in the highly sought-after Risk Management field. We are one of the business leaders in the risk market. We work with a vision to make the world more prosperous, trustworthy, and safe. Deloitte’s clients, primarily based outside of India, are large, complex organizations that constantly evolve and innovate to build better products and services. In the process, they encounter various risks and the work we do to help them address these risks is increasingly important to their success—and to the strength of the economy and public security.
  
  
By joining us, you will get to work with diverse teams of professionals who design, manage, and implement risk-centric solutions across a variety of domains. In the process, you will gain exposure to the risk-centric challenges faced in today’s world by organizations across a range of industry sectors and become subject matter experts in those areas.
  
  
Work you’ll do:
  
  
Our Regulatory, Risk & Forensic Operate professionals help organizations effectively navigate business risks and opportunities — from strategic, reputation, and financial risks to operational and regulatory risks — to gain competitive advantage. We apply our experience in ongoing business operations and corporate lifecycle events to help clients become stronger and more resilient. Our market-leading teams help clients embrace complexity to accelerate performance, disrupt through innovation, and lead in their industries.
  
  
We support clients by delivering Operate services spanning the Regulatory, Risk & Forensic portfolio. We embed continuous advantage through domain, industry, technology / Gen AI, and transformation skills to perform client business functions that manage risk and deliver value-added outcomes.
  
  
As a Consultant within the Testing & Validation Utility, you will individually deliver regulatory, compliance, and controls testing and validation outcomes, along with regulatory reporting, across the end-to-end risk management lifecycle for global clients across industries, with a focus on banking, financial services, and insurance — owning end-to-end execution of assigned work, applying methodology with rigor, and partnering with control owners, process owners, and second-line stakeholders. You will be expected to bring breadth across multiple components and depth in at least two.
  
  
You will perform this work for first-line control owners, second-line risk and compliance functions, and internal audit, following a standard methodology and using analytics and GenAI tools. Typical activities include data sourcing and reconciliation, walkthroughs, population validation, sample selection, evidence review, root cause analysis, workpaper documentation, and reporting of results and remediation status. Specific responsibilities span the following areas:
  
  
**Controls Testing**
Perform end-to-end assessments of the design and operating effectiveness of operational and compliance controls — including walkthroughs, process documentation, test strategy, sample design, and population validation — with full traceability from risk through evidence to conclusion.
  
  

* Perform end-to-end control assessments across operational and compliance controls, including planning, walkthroughs, design and operating effectiveness testing, documentation, and issue follow-up
* Apply risk analysis principles to scope reviews; develop test strategies, sample selection methodology, sample sizing, and rationale; document process flows and key controls
* Prepare reviewer-ready workpapers and draft observations including root-cause analysis, impact assessment, and remediation tracking
* Identify control deficiencies, document them with clear rationale, recommend corrective actions, and re-test where required; track remediation to closure
* Collaborate with control owners, process owners, 2nd Line of Defense partners, and Internal Audit; build reports/dashboards (Excel, Power BI, Tableau) for testing progress and exceptions

**Conformance Testing**
Execute conformance reviews of reports, processes, and controls against published regulatory instructions, internal policies, and procedures; identify variances, perform root cause analysis, and drive remediation.
  
  

* Execute conformance testing of regulatory reports and key business processes against published regulatory instructions, internal policies, procedures, and operating standards (e.g., FFIEC instructions, FR Y-9C glossary, Basel III, MiFID II, FINRA TTRO, Reg YY)
* Perform completeness, timeliness, and accuracy controls; reconcile reports against source data and prior submissions; identify variances and root causes
* Review and enhance process narratives, Operating Procedures, Checklists, and SOPs to ensure they are accurate, current, and aligned with regulator expectations
* Generate MI on conformance results, timeliness, and accuracy; escalate key issues and coordinate IT/operational fixes with business owners
* Support response to internal audit, second-line challenge, and regulatory examinations on conformance topics

**Compliance Testing**
Test the design and operating effectiveness of compliance controls across federal and state consumer protection regulations, BSA/AML, OFAC, sanctions, KYC, and fraud, delivering independent assurance outcomes for the business.
  
  

* Plan and execute compliance testing work programs across consumer and commercial regulations; assess whether controls are designed and operating effectively to comply with applicable laws, regulations, and firm policies
* Conduct routine and ad-hoc compliance testing including forensic testing, transactional testing, and surveillance testing; design test scripts and sampling approaches for high-risk processes
* Apply data analysis tools and analytics to mine populations, identify high-risk transactions, account types, activity patterns, and surface themes across business lines
* Validate Risk and Control Matrices (RCMs), business-unit control testing, and remediation actions; identify control improvement opportunities
* Communicate test results to Compliance, Operational Risk, FLU process owners, and senior stakeholders; identify themes/trends at FLU, control function, and Enterprise level

**Regulatory Reporting QA & Testing**
Perform in-line Quality Assurance and independent testing of regulatory reports to validate data lineage, conformance with reporting instructions, accuracy, completeness, and the effectiveness of report-level controls.
  
  

* Plan and execute end-to-end QA testing across regulatory reporting submissions (FR Y-9C, FR Y-15, FR 2052a, FFIEC, LCR, CCAR, PRA 110, FINREP/COREP, etc.), covering data profiling, completeness, accuracy, conformance with reporting instructions, and control evaluation
* Perform transaction-level testing from point of origin to reporting, including source-to-report data lineage, line item mapping, and validation of underlying products, accounting concepts, data elements, and data flow
* Develop, refresh, and document QA test methodologies including scoping, sample selection, sample sizing rationale, and test scripts for assigned report families
* Prepare reviewer-ready workpapers, draft observations, and conclusions; identify control gaps, document rationale, and recommend remediation
* Coordinate with Report Owners, Finance, Risk, Operations, and Data SMEs to obtain evidence, resolve interpretive questions, and validate findings
* Track issue remediation, validate evidence of closure, and re-test where required; support response to internal audit and regulatory examinations

**Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) and Post-Effectiveness Testing**
Facilitate and execute risk and control self-assessments — identifying inherent risks, evaluating control effectiveness, rating residual risk, and tracking action plans — and perform post-effectiveness testing of key controls, in line with the Operational Risk Management Framework.
  
  

* Facilitate RCSAs for assigned business units and processes: identify inherent risks, evaluate control design and operating effectiveness, assess residual risk, and document RCSA outputs
* Apply enterprise risk taxonomy and control taxonomy; rate risks and controls consistently; map controls to applicable regulations, policies, and standards
* Drive design and execution of post-effectiveness testing for key controls identified in RCSA; validate management's self-assessment ratings and challenge where required
* Track RCSA action plans, control enhancements, and remediation through to closure; partner with 1LoD risk officers, control owners, and 2LoD
* Configure and maintain RCSA records in the GRC platform; produce risk reporting, heat maps, and trend analyses for senior stakeholders

**Issue Management & Remediation Validation**
Validate the completeness and accuracy of issue remediation activities, perform root cause analysis, and assure the sustainability of corrective actions for self-identified, audit, and regulatory issues.
  
  

* Perform issue validation for high-complexity self-identified, audit, and regulatory issues; review and assess individual remediation artifacts for completeness and accuracy
* Partner with issue owners and Issue Execution Officers to incorporate observations into remediation scope prior to issue due date; ensure alignment to enterprise issue management standards and regulatory expectations
* Support completion of issue closure packages with rationale, evidence inventory, and validation conclusions; identify themes in remediation to feed into best practices
* Coordinate end-to-end issue management process: root cause analysis, corrective action development, sustainability testing, and risk mitigation validation
* Provide credible challenge and recommendations to issue owners and leadership; recommend updates to controls, policies, procedures, and risk/control documentation

**Regulatory Reporting**
Alongside testing and validation work, own and execute the preparation, review, and timely submission of financial and non-financial regulatory filings across Banking, Capital Markets, and Investment Management clients — including FFIEC Call Reports, FR Y-series filings, CCAR/DFAST, liquidity and capital reports (LCR, NSFR, FR 2052a), broker-dealer filings (FOCUS, FINRA), and Investment Management reports (Form PF, N-PORT, Form ADV) — with appropriate accuracy, completeness, and audit-ready documentation.
  
  

* Manage end-to-end regulatory reporting activities for assigned report families across Banking (FFIEC Call Reports, FR Y-9C/9LP/9SP, FR Y-14A/Q/M for CCAR/DFAST, FR Y-15, FR 2052a, LCR, NSFR, capital and liquidity reports), Capital Markets (FOCUS Report, FINRA filings, Volcker Rule reporting, large trader reporting), and Investment Management (Form PF, N-PORT, N-CEN, Form ADV, CPO-PQR, 1940 Act and Private Funds, liquidity and derivatives reporting), ensuring compliance with applicable requirements and deadlines
* Prepare, review, and submit regulatory filings to the FRB, OCC, FDIC, SEC, CFTC, FINRA, and international regulators (PRA, FCA, EBA via COREP/FINREP) where applicable; ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with established standards
* Maintain and enhance SOPs, documentation, control frameworks, and audit trails to support audit readiness and regulatory examinations
* Coordinate across Finance Controllership, Treasury, Risk, Compliance, Legal, Operations, Technology, and external service providers throughout the reporting lifecycle; resolve interpretive questions and operational issues
* Support regulatory exams, internal audits, and ad-hoc data requests related to capital, liquidity, financial, and non-financial reporting
* Drive continuous improvement and change-management initiatives to strengthen reporting quality, reduce operational risk, and improve process efficiency

**Root Cause & Thematic Analysis, Testing MI, and KCI/KRI Reporting (across all components)**
Analyze why exceptions occur, surface themes across testing results, and report results and remediation status to control owners, second-line risk and compliance functions, and internal audit.
  
  

* Perform root cause analysis on test exceptions, control deficiencies, and conformance breaks; identify recurring themes across testing cycles and business units and recommend corrective actions
* Build and maintain testing MI, dashboards, and KCI/KRI views (Excel, Power BI, Tableau) covering testing progress, exceptions, and remediation status
* Communicate results and remediation status to control owners, risk and compliance functions, and internal audit; escalate key themes and trends

**Analytics-led & GenAI-enabled Testing (across all components)**

* Use approved AI / GenAI tools (Microsoft 365 Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT / Azure OpenAI, Deloitte-approved AI assistants) to accelerate test-script drafting, walkthrough narrative buildout, policy-to-control mapping, evidence review, exception triage, and report drafting, in line with firm AI usage policies
* Apply prompt-engineering skills (role, context, task, constraints, output format) to generate reliable, audit-friendly outputs; iteratively refine prompts and validate accuracy
* Use SQL, SAS, Python (pandas), Alteryx Designer, KNIME, or Power Query for population validation, sample selection, reconciliations, transaction tracing, and full-population analytical procedures
* Use Power BI, Tableau, or Qlik to build testing dashboards, KCI/KRI views, and stakeholder reporting

Required skills:
  
  

* 4-7 years of relevant experience in controls testing, regulatory reporting QA, conformance testing, compliance testing, RCSA, internal audit, operational risk, SOX, financial crimes, or business process management in a BFSI, other regulated-industry, or consulting environment
* Exposure across the end-to-end risk management lifecycle — Transactions, Conformance, Controls, Compliance, RCSA, and Issue Management — with hands-on delivery in at least two of these components
* Strong understanding of internal control concepts (manual vs. automated controls, preventive vs. detective controls, IPE, SoD, sampling fundamentals)
* Working knowledge of the COSO 2013 framework and US/UK regulatory frameworks (e.g., FR Y-9C, FR Y-15, FR 2052a, LCR, CCAR, PRA 110, Reg YY, BSA/AML, UDAAP, Reg B/Z, FCRA)
* Exposure to regulatory reporting across Banking (FFIEC Call Reports, FR Y-9C, FR Y-14 CCAR/DFAST, FR Y-15, FR 2052a, LCR/NSFR), Capital Markets (FOCUS Report, FINRA filings), and/or Investment Management (Form PF, N-PORT, Form ADV, 1940 Act and Private Funds, derivatives and liquidity reporting) is highly desirable
* Advanced Microsoft Excel (pivots, lookups, conditional logic) and strong working knowledge of Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook
* Working knowledge of, and willingness to use, AI / GenAI tools (Microsoft 365 Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT / Azure OpenAI, or equivalents) for test-script generation, walkthrough narrative buildout, policy-to-control mapping, evidence review, exception triage, and report drafting
* Basic prompt-engineering skills - able to write clear, structured prompts (role, context, task, constraints, output format) and iteratively refine them for reliable, audit-friendly outputs
* Working knowledge of SQL (and exposure to SAS, Python pandas, KNIME, or Power Query) for population validation, sample selection, transaction tracing, reconciliations, and exception analysis
* Hands-on or strong working knowledge of at least one analytical / data-prep tool such as Alteryx Designer, KNIME, or Power Query
* Strong analytical skills with high attention to detail and accuracy
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with ability to document observations and interact with stakeholders across levels
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, manage multiple priorities, and meet deadlines with high-quality standards

Preferred skills:
  
  

* Exposure to BFSI products and processes (banking operations, payments, lending, capital markets, insurance, or investment compliance)
* Exposure to SOX Section 404 and ITGC testing
* Experience with US/UK regulatory requirements across Banking (FR Y-9C, FR Y-14 CCAR/DFAST, FR Y-15, FR 2052a, LCR/NSFR, PRA 110, FFIEC Call Reports, FINREP/COREP), Capital Markets (FOCUS, FINRA filings), and/or Investment Management (Form PF, N-PORT, Form ADV) plus consumer compliance regulations (UDAAP, RESPA, TILA, Reg B/Z, FCRA, SCRA, FDCPA, BSA/AML, OFAC)
* Experience with reporting tools (e.g., Axiom, Vermeg, Moody's, Wolters Kluwer OneSumX) is a plus
* Exposure to GRC platforms (Archer, ServiceNow GRC / IRM, MetricStream, OpenPages, or Workiva)
* Awareness of Continuous Controls Monitoring (CCM) concepts and analytics-driven assurance
* Awareness of Deloitte AI policies and Trustworthy AI frameworks; certifications such as Microsoft AI-900 are a plus
* Pursuing or partially completed certifications such as CIA, CISA, CRMA, CFE, FRM, CAMS, CPA, ACCA, or equivalent
* Public accounting / Big 4 experience in audit or SOX advisory / consulting
* Basic Python or VBA for data wrangling and reconciliation tasks

title: Legal Associate
description:
**Artha Group**

**Legal Associate**

Location: Mumbai, Maharashtra

  

**About Artha Group**

Artha Group is a performance-first investment house managing ₹2,300 crores across domestic and international investment vehicles, including Category I & II AIFs, LLPs, and Private Limited companies. With active investments in 130+ startups, 32+ successful exits, and 10+ renewable energy projects. We operate at the convergence of capital precision and operational depth.

  

**Role Overview**

This is a corporate finance legal role, not a litigation position. The Legal Associate at Artha Group is responsible for the end-to-end legal integrity of the firm's investment transactions, fund documentation, vendor and commercial agreements, and regulatory filings. You will work across every stage of deal execution and fund operations, ensuring that Artha's interests are protected, its obligations are met, and its documentation is precise, enforceable, and defensible. While litigation is not the primary focus, you will be expected to be hands-on with the processes and steps involved in civil disputes, arbitrations, and related proceedings across Artha Group, and in dealing with external litigation counsel, government personnel, officers and departments, and administrative officials, working closely with in-house senior counsel throughout. You will also be a resource for the broader team, guiding analysts and interns on legal processes and building the institutional knowledge that keeps the legal function sharp. This role demands someone who is meticulous, fast, and deeply comfortable operating at the intersection of law, finance, and high-growth business.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

**Investment Agreements and Transaction Structuring**

* Review, negotiate, and finalise Shareholders Agreements, Share Subscription Agreements, term sheets, convertible note agreements, and all other investment-related documentation before they reach the signing stage.
* Ensure that Artha's investor rights, protective provisions, and exit mechanisms are fully secured in every transaction.
* Collaborate with the investment team to structure deals in a legally sound manner, ensuring full compliance with applicable regulatory frameworks.
* Maintain and update standardised term sheet and definitive document templates across fund entities to ensure consistency and efficiency across deals.
Work closely with external legal counsel on complex deal structuring, governance matters, and rights enforcement.  

  

**Fund-Level Legal Documentation**

* Draft, review, and maintain fund-level legal documents including Investment Management Agreements, Private Placement Memoranda, fund formation documents, and ancillary fund agreements across all Artha fund entities.
* Manage legal documentation for new fund launches and entity setups, ensuring all formation and registration requirements are addressed comprehensively from inception through ongoing obligations.
* Coordinate with the compliance team on FIU registrations, SEBI filings, and other regulatory requirements tied to fund structures.
Ensure all fund documentation is current, consistent, and audit-ready at all times.  

  

**Contract Drafting, Review and Negotiation**

* Draft, review, and negotiate vendor agreements, service-level agreements, commercial contracts, MOU agreements, and any other contractual arrangement the firm enters into.
* Conduct legal due diligence on all inbound contracts, identifying risk areas and ensuring that Artha's commercial interests and legal obligations are fully addressed before execution.
Ensure all agreements are enforceable, accurately reflect the agreed commercial terms, and meet the firm's internal compliance protocols.  

  

**External Counsel and Retainer Management**

* Manage the firm's relationships with external legal counsel across panel firms, ensuring retainer arrangements are scoped clearly, tracked diligently, and delivering value.
* Brief external counsel, including senior litigation counsels on dispute matters, efficiently, review their output critically, and ensure that legal spend is purposeful and well-documented.
Maintain a live tracker of all external counsel engagements, retainer terms, billing, and matter status across entities.  

  

**Litigation and Dispute Tracking**

* Track and manage all active litigation and dispute matters in coordination with external litigation counsel and in-house senior counsel, overseeing the procedural steps involved and ensuring timely responses, proper documentation, and resolution.
* Maintain a comprehensive litigation register across all group entities, with clear status updates and escalation flags.
* Liaise with government personnel, officers and departments, and administrative officials on dispute-related and administrative matters, managing the filings, representations, and follow-ups involved.
Prepare internal briefing notes on active matters for senior leadership as required.  

  

**Legal Governance and Risk Management**

* Maintain a legal tracker covering all ongoing matters, regulatory filings, compliance obligations, and document review statuses across entities.
* Proactively identify and flag legal risks associated with investments, contracts, fund structures, and operational decisions before they become issues.
* Provide internal legal advisory support to the investment, operations, and fund teams, ensuring decisions are grounded in sound legal thinking.
Operate under tight deal timelines with precision. The ability to move fast without compromising legal integrity is essential.  

  

**Team Development and Legal Knowledge Building**

* Coach and guide analysts and interns from legal and/or cross-functional teams on the legal processes, document standards and how to approach a specific document or its legal review in the context of venture capital transactions.
* Build and maintain internal legal knowledge resources including playbooks, templates, and process guides that raise the legal competency of the broader team.
Conduct periodic reviews of legal documentation quality across the team and provide structured feedback to ensure standards are consistently met.  

  

**Who You Are**

* A sharp, detail-obsessed corporate finance lawyer with a strong understanding of venture capital deal structuring and fund operations.
* Someone who reads the fine print, spots the gap before it becomes a problem, and closes documentation with the same urgency as the deal itself.
* Comfortable working across multiple matters and entities simultaneously without losing precision or rigour.
* A clear and confident communicator, able to brief investment teams and senior leadership on legal matters without jargon.
Someone who takes pride in building systems and templates that make the whole firm more legally resilient, not just completing individual tasks.  

  

**Qualifications and Experience**

* LLB or LLM from a recognised law school. Bar admission to practice law in India is required.
* 4 or more years of experience in corporate finance, venture capital, private equity, or fund management legal work.
* Deep expertise in investment transaction documents including SHAs, SSAs, convertible notes, term sheets, and IMAs.
* Solid exposure to fund formation, SEBI AIF regulations, and regulatory filings relevant to AIF fund structures.
* Experience managing external counsel relationships and retainer arrangements.
* Strong contract drafting and negotiation skills, with the ability to produce precise, enforceable legal documents independently.
Experience working in a multi-entity group structure is a meaningful advantage.  

  

**Compensation**

* Total Annual Package: Rs. 21,00,000
* Fixed Annual Salary: Rs. 18,00,000 LPA
* Annual Retention Bonus: Rs. 3,00,000, paid at the end of each year

title: Risk Manager / Senior Manager – Infrastructure (InvIT)
description:
**About the Role**

We are looking for an experienced Risk Manager / Senior Manager with strong hands-on exposure to Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and Roads & Highways infrastructure. The incumbent will be responsible for identifying, assessing, monitoring and mitigating financial, operational, commercial and regulatory risks across the InvIT portfolio and underlying project SPVs.

**The role will work closely with**
Finance, Investment Management, Asset Management, Operations, Legal, lenders, rating agencies, the Trustee, NHAI and other external stakeholders to strengthen the overall risk management framework.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Risk Identification & Assessment**

* Identify and assess enterprise, project-level and asset-level risks across road and highway assets.
* Conduct risk assessments for new asset acquisitions, investments, refinancing and operational SPVs.
* Monitor key macro and sectoral risks including traffic, toll revenue, regulatory changes, EPC and O&M contracts.
* Develop risk mitigation plans and track their implementation and effectiveness.

**2. InvIT & Regulatory Risk**

* Monitor compliance with applicable SEBI InvIT Regulations, NHAI concession agreements, lender covenants and other regulatory requirements.
* Work closely with the Investment Manager, Trustee, Valuer and relevant stakeholders on InvIT risk reporting.
* Support risk and commercial due diligence for asset acquisitions, investments, refinancing and divestments.
* Monitor regulatory, contractual and concession-related developments that may impact the portfolio.

**3. Financial & Commercial Risk**

* Analyse traffic risk, toll revenue risk, revenue leakage, O&M cost overruns, interest-rate risk and refinancing risk.
* Perform cash-flow stress testing, scenario analysis and DSCR assessment for road/highway assets.
* Evaluate project and asset-level financial risks and recommend appropriate mitigation strategies.
* Review insurance coverage, claims, business continuity and contingency plans.
* Assess financial and commercial risks associated with BOT, HAM and Toll-based project structures.

**4. Risk Governance & Reporting**

* Develop, maintain and periodically review the Risk Management Framework, Risk Register and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs).
* Establish effective risk monitoring and escalation mechanisms across the InvIT portfolio.
* Prepare risk reports and presentations for the Board, Audit Committee, Investment Committee, lenders and senior management.
* Coordinate with internal audit, external auditors and other assurance functions on risk-related matters.
* Track risk observations, action plans and closure of identified gaps.

**5. Stakeholder Management**

* Liaise with NHAI, lenders, rating agencies, EPC contractors, O&M contractors, Investment Managers, Trustees and other stakeholders on risk-related matters.
* Partner closely with Finance, Legal, Operations, Asset Management and Investment teams.
* Provide risk inputs for strategic, investment and portfolio-management decisions.
* Present risk insights, stress-test outcomes and mitigation plans to senior management and relevant committees.

**Must-Have Qualifications & Experience**

* Education: CA / MBA Finance / M.Com or equivalent qualification.
* 5–10 years of relevant experience in Risk Management, Infrastructure, Project Finance, InvITs, Infrastructure Funds, PE Funds or large Road/Highway Developers.
* Mandatory hands-on experience with InvIT structures and Roads / Highways infrastructure assets.
* Strong understanding of project finance, financial risk assessment and infrastructure project structures.
* Relevant Risk Management certification is preferred.

**Key Skills & Technical Competencies**

• SEBI InvIT Regulations and regulatory compliance

• NHAI policies, concession agreements and highway operations

• BOT / HAM / Toll-based project structures

• Financial modelling and cash-flow risk analysis

• DSCR analysis, stress testing and scenario analysis

• Traffic and toll revenue risk assessment

• Project finance and lender covenant monitoring

• Risk Management Framework, Risk Register and KRI/KPI development

• Governance, Board / Audit Committee reporting and presentation

• Senior stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration

**Preferred Experience**

* Prior experience with listed InvITs.
* Experience working with Investment Managers, Trustees, lenders and / or rating agencies.
* Exposure to asset acquisition / divestment due diligence.
* Experience in refinancing and financial restructuring of infrastructure assets.
* FRM / IRM or other relevant Risk Management certification will be an advantage.

**Ideal Candidate Profile**

The ideal candidate will be a finance / risk professional who combines strong risk management capability with practical understanding of infrastructure assets and InvIT structures. Candidates from
**InvITs, Infrastructure Investment Managers, Road / Highway Developers, Infrastructure Funds, Project Finance teams or Infrastructure-focused PE / Funds**
with hands-on experience in asset-level financial analysis and risk assessment will be highly relevant.

**Candidate Targeting – Priority Backgrounds**

* Listed / unlisted InvITs and Investment Managers
* Road & Highway Developers / concessionaires
* Infrastructure-focused PE / Infrastructure Funds
* Project Finance / Infrastructure Finance teams
* Risk Management teams within infrastructure businesses
* Candidates with combined exposure to InvIT + Roads/Highways + financial modelling / project finance

We are a global financial services group operating in 30 markets with 57 years of unbroken profitability. At Macquarie, you’re empowered to shape a career that is fulfilling and creates value. **About the job**
Google's in-house tax team knows all things corporate tax. Made up of smart, perceptive Googlers with a flair for domestic, international, and sales and use tax, the knowledge and expertise of this team runs deep. You have years of experience in this field and an extensive knowledge of those tax issues most relevant to internet companies. You find ways to work smarter by streamlining and automating our tax processes and systems, and find ways to be both innovative and compliant.

You will directly contribute to optimizing efficiency, clearly articulating tax recommendations and establishing policies that minimize the company's tax exposure.

title: Senior Data Protection Consultant
description:
**About The Job**

**Location**
: Noida

**Experience**
: 4–6 Years

**Employment Type**
: Full-Time

Immediate Joiners or candidates serving a notice period of up to 15 days will be preferred.

**About the Role**

We are looking for a Senior Consultant to join our growing Privacy Consulting practice. You will turn the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), the IT Act and global frameworks such as GDPR and CCPA/CPRA into practical, engineering-friendly action. You will run privacy assessments, build RoPAs and data inventories, conduct DPIAs, shape data privacy agreements and Data Fiduciary to Data Processor arrangements, and work with product and technology teams to make sure privacy requirements are actually implemented in systems and processes, not just documented

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the overall DPDP implementation roadmap, project plan, timelines, milestones and deliverables.
* Conduct privacy gap assessments and track remediation across business entities and functions.
* Lead personal data mapping, Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs), Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) and Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs).
* Develop and implement privacy policies, procedures, consent management, data principal rights, grievance handling and breach management processes.
* Coordinate with IT, Information Security, Legal, HR, Procurement, Marketing and business teams to drive compliance.
* Manage third-party privacy assessments, vendor DPAs, contractual requirements and privacy risks.
* Evaluate and coordinate implementation of privacy management tools and automation solutions.
* Conduct privacy awareness and training programs and support audits and regulatory compliance reviews.
* Prepare management dashboards, progress reports, risk registers and periodic updates for senior leadership.

**Required Skills and Experience**

* Strong working knowledge of the DPDP Act, 2023 and applicable DPDP Rules.
* Hands-on experience in end-to-end privacy compliance implementation and consulting.
* Practical knowledge of RoPA, DFDs, DPIAs, consent management, data principal rights and third-party privacy risk management.
* Strong project management, stakeholder coordination, documentation and communication skills.
* Bachelor's or master's degree in IT, Cybersecurity, Law, Management, or a related field.
* Privacy certifications such as CIPP/A, CIPM, CDPSE, or DSCI privacy certifications are preferred.
* Knowledge of ISO 27701, ISO 27001 and GDPR is an added advantage.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Law, Computer Science, Information Security, Engineering, or a related discipline.
* LLB/LLM, B.Tech, B.E., MCA, or equivalent qualifications are preferred.
* Candidates with a background in Privacy, Cybersecurity, Risk, or Compliance Consulting will be given preference.

title: Contracts Operations Specialist Senior Associate
description:
**Your Journey at Crowe Starts Here:**
At Crowe, you can build a meaningful and rewarding career. With real flexibility to balance work with life moments, you’re trusted to deliver results and make an impact. We embrace you for who you are, care for your well-being, and nurture your career. Everyone has equitable access to opportunities for career growth and leadership. Over our 80-year history, delivering excellent service through innovation has been a core part of our DNA across our audit, tax, and consulting groups. That’s why we continuously invest in innovative ideas, such as AI-enabled insights and technology-powered solutions, to enhance our services. Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.
  
  
**Job Description:**
**What It Means To Be a Consultant At Crowe**
Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. In this role, you will continuously learn, collaborate across teams, and explore how tools, including emerging AI capabilities, can improve efficiency, insights, and client outcomes.
  
  
As you grow, you’ll also begin to take ownership of client relationships, contribute to account strategy, and support the delivery of high-impact work. Developing a sense of account leadership, including understanding client needs, ensuring delivery excellence, and building trusted partnerships, is part of what sets successful consultants apart.
  
  
Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence.
  
  
**Job Profile Summary**
The Contracts Operations Specialist (Senior Associate) supports the day-to-day operations of the Contracts pillar within Consulting Quality & Risk Management. Based in Noida, this role executes standardized contract intake, creation, and administration activities, and provides extended-hours coverage that keeps the contracting queue moving across time zones. This is a fast-paced, high-volume environment: the person in this role will manage competing deadlines, shift priorities quickly, and maintain accuracy and compliance under time pressure.
  
  
This position requires strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to communicate effectively across a distributed, US-and-India team. The Specialist works closely with Contracts Managers, the Assistant Director, and cross-functional stakeholders (Legal, Risk, and business-unit leadership) to ensure efficient contract lifecycle management.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Execute standardized contract intake, drafting, and creation activities, including simple and time-sensitive requests, in accordance with firm policies and regulations.
* Monitor shared mailbox and administer day-to-day workflow: uploads, execution steps, opportunity close initiation, Legal review requests, and redlines.
* Support administration of the contract management system (Icertis) to ensure data integrity, technical document setup, accurate reporting, and timely status updates.
* Proactively monitor contract movement and identify stalled, slow-moving, or stopped matters for resolution or escalation.
* Help identify and implement improvements to contract management processes, working with Contracts leadership to streamline workflows and reduce inefficiencies.
* Partner with internal stakeholders — including Legal, Risk Management, Client-facing teams, and business-unit leaders — to ensure alignment on contract documentation and engagement processes.
* Assist in the preparation of contract-related reports, ensuring accurate data capture and up-to-date documentation.
* Maintain clear handoffs and documentation to support seamless coordination with U.S.-based team members.
* Support training on contract management workflows and technology tools as needed.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience in business, law, or a related field.
* 3–5 years of experience in contract administration, contract management, legal support, or operations, ideally within a consulting or professional services environment.
* Working Hours: 12:00 PM IST - 9:00 PM IST
* Familiarity with contract management systems, particularly Icertis.
* Proficient in the Microsoft Office suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, D365), ServiceNow, & AI productivity tools.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet critical deadlines while maintaining accuracy and quality.
* Team-oriented, with experience working with diverse teams.
* Ability to leverage available resources and contribute through others.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively across teams, time zones, and levels of seniority.
* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines in a high-paced, high-volume environment.
* High attention to detail and strong organizational skills.
* Strong organizational, interpersonal, and presentation skills.
* Demonstrated professionalism and confidentiality when handling sensitive information.
* US Collaboration: willingness to work 4–5 hours of daily live overlap with U.S. Eastern Time (EST/EDT) teams for standups, handovers, and real-time collaboration to start.
* Candidate must have reliable means of commuting to and from local office.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience supporting projects or workflows related to contract management.
* Ability to identify areas for process improvement and propose practical solutions.
* Understanding of professional services business practices and priorities.
* Experience working in a global capability center or similar distributed operating model supporting U.S.-based stakeholders.

**Work Environment**
This role sits within a growing, fast-paced Contracts function supporting a high volume of consulting engagements. Priorities can shift quickly, and the Specialist should be comfortable balancing routine, standardized work with time-sensitive requests. The role is based in Noida, India, and works to provide extended coverage aligned with U.S. business-day overlap. US collaboration is required with shift flexibility possible upon demonstration of functional proficiency.
  
  
We expect the candidate to uphold Crowe’s values of Care, Trust, Courage, and Stewardship. These values define who we are. We expect all of our people to act ethically and with integrity at all times.
  
  
**Our Benefits:**
At Crowe, we know that great people are what makes a great firm. We value our people and offer employees a comprehensive benefits package. Learn more about what working at Crowe can mean for you!
  
  
**How You Can Grow:**
We will nurture your talent in an inclusive culture that values diversity. You will have the chance to meet on a consistent basis with your Career Coach that will guide you in your career goals and aspirations. Learn more about where talent can prosper!
  
  
**More about Crowe:**
Crowe Capability Center – India, operating under the legal entity C3 India Delivery Centre LLP (formerly known as Crowe Horwath IT Services LLP) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Crowe LLP (U.S.A.), a public accounting, consulting and technology firm with offices around the world. Crowe LLP is an independent member firm of Crowe Global, one of the largest global accounting networks in the world. The network consists of more than 200 independent accounting and advisory firms in more than 130 countries around the world.
  
  
Crowe does not accept unsolicited candidates, referrals or resumes from any staffing agency, recruiting service, sourcing entity or any other third-party paid service at any time. Any referrals, resumes or candidates submitted to Crowe, or any employee or owner of Crowe without a pre-existing agreement signed by both parties covering the submission will be considered the property of Crowe, and free of charge.
  
  
We are committed to a merit-based hiring process, evaluating all candidates consistently using objective, job-related criteria such as relevant experience, demonstrated skills, measurable impact, and alignment with the role’s responsibilities, and making employment decisions in a fair and inclusive manner free from discrimination.

title: Associate Legal Counsel
description:

Looking ahead, we are building the team and foundation to drive another 2x growth in 2027 as we accelerate toward our $100M goal.

This is Loop's first dedicated legal hire and an important step in building the legal function. You will work directly with the Chief of Staff, own day-to-day legal execution, and build the templates, playbooks and SOPs that protect the company as it scales. We are looking for someone who wants to build with the team over the long term and retain ownership of the systems they create. This position will work on derisking and actively work with Sales, marketing, product, and finance team to remove legal roadblocks.

**Responsibilities**

* Commercial contracts. Draft, review and negotiate SaaS MSAs, Order Forms, DPAs, NDAs, vendor, partner and other business  
  agreements.
* Merchant negotiations. Lead issue-based calls with merchants and their counsel, understand the commercial concern, explain  
  Loop's position and agree workable fallbacks.
* Contract standards. Maintain templates and clause positions for legal or regulatory changes; periodically redesign the contract suite to remove inconsistencies, reflect negotiation history and improve clarity.

* Product and consumer rules. Assess cookie and tracking requirements, API and data-access terms, and subscription, auto-renewal and cancellation rules across relevant markets; translate findings into product and contract actions.
* Security and assurance. Partner with Engineering, Security and Operations on PCI DSS responsibilities, SOC 2 readiness, customer security reviews and the legal evidence needed for audits.
* IP employment and general advisory. Support IP protection and licensing, HR policies, employment and consultant documents, and routine business contract reviews.
* Legal operations and risk discovery. Create intake, approval, escalation, repository and obligation-tracking SOPs. Proactively identify legal risks that the business has not yet considered, rank them and drive practical mitigation with internal teams or external counsel.

**Ideal Profile**

* Law degree from a recognized institution and 2 to 5 years of relevant experience.
* Hands-on commercial contract drafting and negotiation experience; SaaS, technology or in-house exposure is strongly preferred.
* Ability to research unfamiliar multi-jurisdictional questions, separate legal requirements from business preferences and give a clear recommendation.
* Comfort speaking directly with merchants, business teams and technical stakeholders.
* Strong drafting discipline, attention to detail and judgment on when to accept, negotiate or escalate risk.
* Ownership mindset

**Perks**

  

* Annual Leaves
* Free lunch and snacks
* Annual company retreat

title: Manager - Regulatory and Commercial
description:
**About the Role**

This role is responsible for supporting the team by executing essential regulatory tasks, initiating compliance procedures, and maintaining effective communication both internally and externally. This role is pivotal role for ensuring smooth operation within the regulatory framework of the power.

**Responsibilities**

**Policy Advocacy and Regulatory Compliance**

* Assist in monitoring policy developments and regulatory changes that may impact the organization's operations.
* Support efforts to ensure that the organization's practices align with current regulations and legislative requirements.
* Help gather information and contribute to internal discussions on how sector regulations and government interventions may affect the organization.
* Aid in the preparation of compliance documentation and reports, ensuring that all business activities adhere to regulatory standards.
* Stay up-to-date with changes in legislation and regulatory requirements, and assist in communicating these changes to relevant departments within the organization.

**Due Diligence and Research**

* Conduct due diligence for mergers and acquisitions (M&A) from a regulatory perspective, preparing notes and presentations for the Business Development (BD) team.
* Perform regulatory research by reviewing updates from regulatory websites such as the Ministry of Power (MOP) to identify new draft notifications, regulations, or policies.
* Support compliance efforts by contributing to the development and maintenance of internal controls and procedures.

**Litigation Coordination and Petition Drafting**

* Coordinate with advocates, briefing them on regulatory litigation matters, and ensure timely submission of petitions.
* Brief legal firms on specific cases and assist with in-house drafting of petitions by compiling information and ensuring logical presentation.
* If law firms are drafting petitions, provide a first draft or a comprehensive information bucket for their use.
* Manage administrative tasks related to litigation, such as obtaining certified copies of legal documents.

**Internal MIS and Reporting**

* Prepare internal MIS reports listing cases pending before the court, categorizing them by criticality, forum, and plant, and disseminate to promoters.
* Compile monthly reports detailing judgments passed, new guidelines from state or central regulators, and other relevant updates.
* Conduct weekly review meetings to discuss regulatory cases and develop strategies based on direction from the Head/ Chief of Energy Regulatory and Commercial group (ERCG).
* Monitor the progression of regulatory cases, keeping detailed records of filings, hearings, and judgments.
* Assist in the preparation and organization of legal documents required for regulatory submissions and correspondence.

**Billing and Revenue Management**

* Manage the comprehensive management of revenue, ensuring all billing activities in accordance with the SOP for Power Sale align with organizational financial objectives.
* Collect necessary information and inputs for billing, coordinating with internal and external stakeholders.
* Issue accurate and timely invoices to customers or power procurers
* Monitor payments to ensure they are received by the due date.
* Maintain and update all invoicing information on the Ministry of Power portal, responding to any disputes raised by customers.
* Continuously monitor replies and communications within the portal.
* Verify customer information and address anomalies if any to prevent delays.

**Payment Tracking and Dispute Resolution**

* Proactively track payments and initiate letters of credit (LC) to encash funds when payments are delayed.
* In the event of a dispute, ensure that customers pay 85% of the invoice amount as per contract, providing justification for the payment.
* Manage stay orders from the regulatory committee, waiting for resolutions before proceeding with collections.
* Communicate with banks regarding payment statuses, letter of credit (LC) issuances.
* Ensure the original letter of credit (LC) value is restored within 7 days if utilized.

**Portal Management**

* Update the Payment Security Portal (PSA) and Praapti portal with necessary information. For e.g. letter of credit (LC) availability.
* Monitor power curtailment actions by the System Operator as mandated by the Ministry of Power.
* Document payment statuses and upload all bills to the Praapti portal, ensuring accurate and timely updates of procurer details.
* Enforce restrictions on short-term power purchases for entities with outstanding payments beyond 75 days as recorded in the Praapti portal.
* Interact with the state load dispatch center, central dispatch, and Ministry of Power as necessary, ensuring compliance with operational guidelines.

**Financial Reporting and Reconciliation**

* Prepare MIS reports detailing expected revenue, expenses for each customer, due bills, and collection targets, comparing actual receipts against targets.
* Conduct quarterly or annual reconciliations of bills admitted, signed off, and payments made, reporting reconciliation status.
* Draft replies for customer correspondence and ensure accurate entry of bills into the SAP system as payments are made.

**Qualifications**

**Educational Qualification**

* B.E./ B.Tech/ Masters ( Power Management, related field), Additional Certifications in regulatory affairs or compliance preferred

**Work Experience (Range of years)**

* Minimum 5 years of experience in regulatory compliance, preferably in power and transmission or related field.

**Preferred Industry**

* Background in the power and energy sector with exposure to power and transmission industry, with an understanding of regulatory challenges and compliance mechanisms.
